    • Scope note — granularities
    • File Structure
      • Task 1: Typed models for the ideal composite
      • Task 2: Resolve per-bucket winners from the campaign report JSON
      • Task 3: Economics composite from the winners' attributed trades
      • Task 4: Score the stitched series once (scores composite)

    ARCHIVED 2026-07-11 — DONE, then SUPERSEDED. All tasks implemented; the single-file ideal report this plan built was replaced by 20260710_CAMPAIGN_IDEAL_REPORT_REDESIGN (per-group files + episode timeline).

    Campaign Ideal Composite Report (Part B) Implementation Plan

    For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

    Goal: A separate campaign_ideal_report.py that composes, per regime bucket, the winning strategy into one time-ordered hindsight "regime router" run over the whole period, for both routings (by economics PnL and by scores) and all seven taxonomy views, reporting the composite absolute net PnL, compounded %-return and Sharpe, per-regime contribution, and a once-scored stitched signal quality.

    Architecture: The composite reuses Part A's campaign_report.json for winner selection (winner strategy names per bucket) and its experiments[] array to map each name to its backtest_session_id / trial_id. It re-fetches the winners' real closed trades and per-bar predictions through the shared helpers (never inline SQL/parquet), attributes each trade to a regime by its entry bar exactly as the economics layer does (join_to_regime_series on opened_at), and scores a single stitched per-bar prediction series once (aggregate_model_quality_by_regime over a one-value group column). Pure composition logic lives in a new testable module; the CLI script is a thin IO orchestrator plus a renderer.

    Tech Stack: Python 3.11, Polars, frozen slotted dataclasses, pytest, the rainbow.* editable packages.

    Global Constraints

    • Every touched Python file must pass, with no suppressions (# type: ignore / # noqa / pylint: disable are forbidden — fix the root cause):
    • .venv/bin/ruff check <file>
    • MYPYPATH="$(ls -d modules/*/src | tr '\n' ':')" .venv/bin/mypy --strict <file> (MYPYPATH, not PYTHONPATH — required for this repo's src-layout namespace packages)
    • .venv/bin/pyright <file>
    • .venv/bin/pylint <file> — score ≥ 9.5
    • Run tests for scripts/* modules with .venv/bin/python -m pytest (repo root on sys.path so from scripts.experiments... resolves). The IDE/LSP may show reportMissingImports for scripts.* in test files — that is an LSP false positive; the pyright CLI is the gate and resolves them.
    • Line length ≤ 120; 4-space indent; UTF-8; PEP8; English everywhere; type hints on every signature; complete docstrings; comments explain the non-obvious why; no plan/task/phase references in code, comments, docstrings, docs or commit messages.
    • Typed objects flow between functions; a model becomes a dict only at the JSON persistence boundary.
    • No inline DB queries and no inline parquet reads. Only the shared helpers touch the DB and parquets: fetch_closed_trades, fetch_backtest_session_metrics (rainbow.core.helpers.reports); prepare_prediction_parquet_for_trial, load_prediction_parquet_columns (rainbow.core.helpers.reports); read_regime_series, join_to_regime_series (rainbow.data_processing.helpers.regime); regime series ensured via scripts.experiments.common.regime_reporting.ensure_regime_series.
    • Formatting reuses the existing fmt_* family from rainbow.core.helpers.reports (fmt_money, fmt_pct, fmt_decimal, fmt_count, fmt_sharpe, fmt_f1, fmt_js). Reuse canonical column labels already in the legend registry; register a new label only if genuinely new. Never a fallback legend (Report field named …) — a publication blocker.
    • Sharpe reuses compute_sharpe_ratio / annualized_sharpe from rainbow.common.helpers (fixed sqrt(252)); it expects per-trade returns already normalized by initial equity (net_pnl / initial_equity).
    • Capital base for %/Sharpe is each winning session's persisted initial_equity (BacktestSessionMetrics.initial_equity). It is uniform across the campaign; if two contributing sessions report different non-null initial_equity, the script stops with an error rather than mixing bases.
    • The composite is a hindsight, in-sample ceiling (winners chosen on the same period's results). Every rendered composite total carries that caveat label.
    • Header carries the DB as-of date, the last-regenerated timestamp and the exact regenerate command (build_regenerate_section). Publishing follows stage → verify → publish (a human workflow, out of code scope here); never regenerate onto a canonical path.
    • Attribution, not re-simulation: a trade's whole realized PnL is credited to its entry-bar regime's winner. This is an approximation and is documented as such.
    • Do not commit or run long processes without explicit instruction.

    Scope note — granularities

    The design speaks of "27, 9 and 3". Part A's campaign_report.json exposes seven taxonomy views (the 27-state, three 9-state views, three 3-state views). The composite is produced for every view the regime payload carries (all seven), since each view is a valid routing granularity and its winners are already present. No view is special-cased.

    File Structure

    • scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_types.py — create: typed models for the composite (winner resolution, economics composite, scores composite, routing/view/section aggregates, top payload).
    • scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_tables.py — create: pure builders — winner resolution from the report JSON, the economics composite from fetched trades, the scores composite from a stitched frame, the per-bar prediction stitcher, and JSON serialization.
    • scripts/experiments/campaigns/campaign_ideal_report.py — create: the CLI orchestrator — reads campaign_report.json, ensures the regime series per section, re-fetches trades / predictions / initial_equity through the shared helpers, calls the pure builders, and writes the Markdown + JSON with a header and regenerate command.
    • scripts/experiments/tests/test_campaign_ideal_tables.py — create: unit tests for the pure builders.
    • The pytest test path scripts/experiments/tests is already registered in pyproject.toml (from Part A).

    Create scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_types.py:

    """Typed models for the campaign ideal-composite ("regime router", hindsight) report.

The composite picks, per regime bucket, the winning strategy under a routing (by realized net PnL, or by
signal scores) and stitches those winners into one time-ordered run over the whole period. These frozen
dataclasses are the single in-memory representation both the Markdown renderer and the JSON serializer read,
so the two outputs cannot drift. Every total is an in-sample, hindsight ceiling.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RegimeWinner:
    """The winning strategy for one regime bucket under one routing, with its resolved identity."""

    regime: str
    strategy: str
    backtest_session_id: int | None
    trial_id: int | None
    net_pnl: float | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CompositeEconomics:
    """The stitched economics of one routing: summed net PnL, return, Sharpe and per-regime contribution."""

    total_net_pnl: float
    return_pct: float | None
    sharpe: float | None
    trade_count: int
    per_regime_net_pnl: tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CompositeScores:
    """The once-scored signal quality of one routing's stitched per-bar prediction series."""

    bars: int
    accuracy: float
    entry_precision: float
    entry_recall: float
    entry_f1: float
    macro_f1: float
    js_divergence: float


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RoutingComposite:
    """One routing (by PnL or by scores): its per-bucket winners and the two composite lenses."""

    routing: str
    winners: tuple[RegimeWinner, ...]
    economics: CompositeEconomics | None
    scores: CompositeScores | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class IdealViewComposite:
    """Both routings' composites for a single taxonomy view."""

    taxonomy: str
    by_pnl: RoutingComposite
    by_scores: RoutingComposite


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class IdealSectionComposite:
    """All seven taxonomy composites for one ``(symbol, labeling config)`` section."""

    symbol: str
    labeling_config_hash: str
    views: tuple[IdealViewComposite, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CampaignIdealPayload:
    """The whole ideal-composite analysis: one section per ``(symbol, labeling config)`` group."""

    sections: tuple[IdealSectionComposite, ...]
    initial_equity: float | None

    assert index["alpha"]["trial_id"] == 10

    Create scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_tables.py:

    """Pure builders for the campaign ideal-composite report.

No database or parquet access happens here. The CLI orchestrator fetches the winners' trades, predictions
and initial equity through the shared helpers and hands already-loaded Polars frames and parsed JSON to
these functions, which compose the typed models the renderer and JSON serializer consume.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Any

from scripts.experiments.common.campaign_ideal_types import RegimeWinner

_ROUTING_BY_PNL = "by_pnl"
_ROUTING_BY_SCORES = "by_scores"


def build_name_index(report: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Map each campaign experiment's strategy name to its report row (carrying the resolvable ids).

    The last row wins on a duplicate name; the campaign runner does not guarantee unique names, so a
    duplicate silently collapses to one identity (documented limitation, acceptable for the hindsight
    composite).
    """
    experiments = report.get("experiments") or []
    index: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for row in experiments:
        name = row.get("name")
        if isinstance(name, str) and name:
            index[name] = dict(row)
    return index


def resolve_winners(
    winner_rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    routing: str,
    name_index: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
) -> tuple[RegimeWinner, ...]:
    """Resolve the per-bucket winning strategy and its ids for one routing.

    ``by_pnl`` reads ``best_economics_strategy`` / ``best_economics_net_pnl``; ``by_scores`` reads
    ``best_scores_strategy`` (net PnL stays ``None``). A bucket whose winner name is missing, or absent from
    the name index, contributes no winner.
    """
    strategy_key = "best_economics_strategy" if routing == _ROUTING_BY_PNL else "best_scores_strategy"
    winners: list[RegimeWinner] = []
    for row in winner_rows:
        strategy = row.get(strategy_key)
        if not isinstance(strategy, str) or strategy not in name_index:
            continue
        identity = name_index[strategy]
        net_pnl_raw = row.get("best_economics_net_pnl") if routing == _ROUTING_BY_PNL else None
        winners.append(
            RegimeWinner(
                regime=str(row["regime"]),
                strategy=strategy,
                backtest_session_id=_opt_int(identity.get("backtest_session_id")),
                trial_id=_opt_int(identity.get("trial_id")),
                net_pnl=None if net_pnl_raw is None else float(net_pnl_raw),
            )
        )
    return tuple(winners)


def _opt_int(value: Any) -> int | None:
    """Coerce a JSON scalar to an optional int."""
    return None if value is None else int(value)

    def build_economics_composite(
    included_trades: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner],
    initial_equity: float | None,
) -> CompositeEconomics | None:
    """Compose the economics of a routing from its winners' entry-attributed trades.

    ``included_trades`` holds one row per real trade credited to the composite (a winner's trade whose
    entry-bar regime equals the bucket it won). The headline is the absolute summed net PnL; the compounded
    ``return_pct`` and ``sharpe`` normalize each trade's net PnL by the shared ``initial_equity``. The
    per-regime contribution is ordered by the winners' order so the money map reads regime by regime.
    """
    if included_trades.height == 0:
        return None
    net_pnls = [float(value) for value in included_trades["net_pnl"].to_list()]
    total_net_pnl = float(sum(net_pnls))
    return_pct = None if not initial_equity else total_net_pnl / float(initial_equity)
    sharpe = (
        None
        if not initial_equity
        else compute_sharpe_ratio([value / float(initial_equity) for value in net_pnls])
    )
    per_regime_totals = {
        str(row["regime"]): float(row["net_pnl"])
        for row in included_trades.group_by("regime").agg(pl.col("net_pnl").sum().alias("net_pnl")).to_dicts()
    }
    per_regime_net_pnl = tuple(
        (winner.regime, per_regime_totals[winner.regime])
        for winner in winners
        if winner.regime in per_regime_totals
    )
    return CompositeEconomics(
        total_net_pnl=total_net_pnl,
        return_pct=return_pct,
        sharpe=sharpe,
        trade_count=included_trades.height,
        per_regime_net_pnl=per_regime_net_pnl,
    )

    Append to campaign_ideal_tables.py (add from rainbow.model_trainer.helpers.regime_model_quality import aggregate_model_quality_by_regime and the type CompositeScores):

    _STITCHED_GROUP_COLUMN = "composite"
_STITCHED_GROUP_VALUE = "ALL"


def build_scores_composite(stitched: pl.DataFrame) -> CompositeScores | None:
    """Score a stitched per-bar prediction series once against the labels.

    Scores (accuracy, entry precision/recall/F1, macro F1, JS) are confusion-matrix ratios and cannot be
    averaged across buckets, so the whole stitched series is scored in one pass by grouping on a single
    constant column — ``aggregate_model_quality_by_regime`` then loops exactly once and returns one row over
    all bars.
    """
    if stitched.height == 0:
        return None
    grouped = stitched.with_columns(pl.lit(_STITCHED_GROUP_VALUE).alias(_STITCHED_GROUP_COLUMN))
    scored = aggregate_model_quality_by_regime(grouped, regime_column=_STITCHED_GROUP_COLUMN)
    row = scored.row(0, named=True)
    return CompositeScores(
        bars=int(row["count"]),
        accuracy=float(row["accuracy"]),
        entry_precision=float(row["entry_precision"]),
        entry_recall=float(row["entry_recall"]),
        entry_f1=float(row["entry_f1"]),
        macro_f1=float(row["macro_f1"]),
        js_divergence=float(row["js_divergence"]),
    )

            "taxonomy_3_trend": ["TRENDING", "TRENDING", "RANGING"],
        }
    )
    winners = (RegimeWinner("TRENDING", "beta", 200, 20, None),
               RegimeWinner("RANGING", "alpha", 100, 10, None))
    included = build_included_trades(joined, taxonomy="taxonomy_3_trend", winners=winners)
    # alpha's TRENDING trade (999) is dropped: TRENDING's winner is beta, not alpha.
    assert sorted(included["net_pnl"].to_list()) == [-40.0, 100.0]
    assert set(included["regime"].to_list()) == {"TRENDING", "RANGING"}


def test_build_stitched_predictions_routes_each_bar_to_its_bucket_winner() -> None:
    """Each bar takes the prediction of its bucket's winner; bars without a winner/prediction drop out."""
    labels_with_regime = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "timestamp": [datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC), datetime(2024, 1, 2, tzinfo=UTC)],
            "label": ["LONG", "SHORT"],
            "taxonomy_3_trend": ["TRENDING", "RANGING"],

    )

               RegimeWinner("RANGING", "alpha", 100, 10, None))
    predictions = {
        "beta": pl.DataFrame({"timestamp": [datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)], "signal": ["LONG"]}),
        "alpha": pl.DataFrame({"timestamp": [datetime(2024, 1, 2, tzinfo=UTC)], "signal": ["NONE"]}),
    }
    stitched = build_stitched_predictions(
        labels_with_regime, taxonomy="taxonomy_3_trend", winners=winners,
        predictions_by_strategy=predictions,
    )
    rows = {(r["label"], r["signal"]) for r in stitched.to_dicts()}
    assert rows == {("LONG", "LONG"), ("SHORT", "NONE")}

    def _winner_by_bucket(winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map each bucket code to its winning strategy name."""
    return {winner.regime: winner.strategy for winner in winners}


def build_included_trades(
    joined_trades: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    taxonomy: str,
    winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Keep only the trades a routing credits to the composite for one taxonomy view.

    A trade is included when the winner of its entry-bar bucket (``joined_trades[taxonomy]``) is the trade's
    own strategy, which is exactly the attribution the economics layer uses (entry-bar regime). The returned
    frame carries the bucket as ``regime`` plus ``strategy``, ``net_pnl`` and ``session_id``.
    """
    winner_by_bucket = _winner_by_bucket(winners)
    if joined_trades.height == 0 or taxonomy not in joined_trades.columns:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema={"regime": pl.Utf8, "strategy": pl.Utf8, "net_pnl": pl.Float64,
                                    "session_id": pl.Int64})
    mapping_frame = pl.DataFrame(
        {"regime": list(winner_by_bucket.keys()), "winner_strategy": list(winner_by_bucket.values())}
    )
    return (
        joined_trades.rename({taxonomy: "regime"})
        .drop_nulls("regime")
        .join(mapping_frame, on="regime", how="inner")
        .filter(pl.col("strategy") == pl.col("winner_strategy"))
        .select("regime", "strategy", "net_pnl", "session_id")
    )


def build_stitched_predictions(
    labels_with_regime: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    taxonomy: str,
    winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner],
    predictions_by_strategy: Mapping[str, pl.DataFrame],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Build the routed per-bar ``(label, signal)`` series for one taxonomy view.

    Each bar's bucket selects the winner strategy; that winner's prediction ``signal`` at the bar's
    timestamp is taken. Bars whose bucket has no winner, or whose winner has no prediction at that bar, drop
    out (scored over the bars actually routed and predicted).
    """
    winner_by_bucket = _winner_by_bucket(winners)
    if labels_with_regime.height == 0 or taxonomy not in labels_with_regime.columns:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema={"label": pl.Utf8, "signal": pl.Utf8})
    per_strategy_frames: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
    base = labels_with_regime.rename({taxonomy: "regime"}).drop_nulls("regime")
    for bucket, strategy in winner_by_bucket.items():
        predictions = predictions_by_strategy.get(strategy)
        if predictions is None or predictions.height == 0:
            continue
        bucket_bars = base.filter(pl.col("regime") == bucket).select("timestamp", "label")
        stitched_bucket = bucket_bars.join(
            predictions.select("timestamp", "signal"), on="timestamp", how="inner"
        ).select("label", "signal")
        if stitched_bucket.height > 0:
            per_strategy_frames.append(stitched_bucket)
    if not per_strategy_frames:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema={"label": pl.Utf8, "signal": pl.Utf8})
    return pl.concat(per_strategy_frames, how="vertical")

    Append to campaign_ideal_tables.py (add from dataclasses import asdict and the remaining type imports):

    _HINDSIGHT_CAVEAT = (
    "In-sample hindsight ceiling: winners are chosen on the same period's results, so every total is an "
    "optimistic upper bound, not an achievable forward return."
)


def _routing_to_dict(routing: RoutingComposite) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize one routing's winners and both composite lenses."""
    return {
        "routing": routing.routing,
        "winners": [asdict(winner) for winner in routing.winners],
        "economics": None if routing.economics is None else asdict(routing.economics),
        "scores": None if routing.scores is None else asdict(routing.scores),
    }


def campaign_ideal_payload_to_dict(payload: CampaignIdealPayload) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize the typed ideal-composite payload into JSON-safe primitives with the hindsight caveat."""
    return {
        "hindsight": _HINDSIGHT_CAVEAT,
        "initial_equity": payload.initial_equity,
        "sections": [
            {
                "symbol": section.symbol,
                "labeling_config_hash": section.labeling_config_hash,
                "views": [
                    {
                        "taxonomy": view.taxonomy,
                        "by_pnl": _routing_to_dict(view.by_pnl),
                        "by_scores": _routing_to_dict(view.by_scores),
                    }
                    for view in section.views
                ],
            }
            for section in payload.sections
        ],
    }

    Note: asdict(CompositeEconomics) serializes per_regime_net_pnl (a tuple of tuples) into a list of 2-item lists — JSON-safe.
